head.title: Getting to the pavilion
head.lede: The pavilion sits inside the Arsenale, about an eight-minute walk from the crossing at the Piraeus Lion. Guests by water taxi enter from the North Lagoon.

about.title: About
about.p1: The Armenian Pavilion unfolds across two sites within the historic Arsenale of Venice—a 5,000-square-foot interior studio and a monumental outdoor sculpture at the gates of the complex.
about.p2: Together they form a single constellation: a place for study, for work, to create, share, and exhibit. Over six months the Pavilion operates not as a static exhibition but as a living workshop—open, evolving, and built in real time.
studio.title: The Studio
studio.p1: Tesa 41 is the primary studio and exhibition space for the Armenian Pavilion—5,000 square feet of expansive industrial volume within the Arsenale that functions as the operational and conceptual heart of the project.
studio.p2: Here, the Pavilion operates as a working studio rather than a static exhibition—a place of continuous making, stacking, dismantling, and rebuilding. The interior volume allows the work to expand horizontally and vertically, accommodating both monumental arrangements and intimate moments of material attention.
studio.p3: Defined by scale, clarity, and architectural restraint, the space is built for sustained fabrication, assembly, and reconfiguration across the full duration of the Biennale.
studio.p4: Tesa 41 anchors the Pavilion physically and philosophically—establishing the studio as the artwork itself.
outdoor.title: The Outdoor Piece
outdoor.p1: The outdoor artwork will be installed at the historic crossing grounds near the Piraeus Lion, one of the most recognized landmarks marking the approach to the Arsenale. Positioned at a critical pedestrian junction, this site receives exceptionally high foot traffic throughout the six-month exhibition period.
outdoor.p2: Visitors moving between venues, crossing the bridge into the Arsenale, and navigating the surrounding waterfront naturally converge here. The Armenian Pavilion lies less than a ten-minute walk from this point, making the installation both a threshold and a directional marker—an early encounter that orients audiences toward the Pavilion.
outdoor.p3: A freestanding, architecturally scaled form—functioning simultaneously as sculpture, signal, and prelude.
arsenale.title: Arsenale Militare
arsenale.p1: The Arsenale di Venezia is one of the largest and oldest shipbuilding complexes in the world. Founded in the 12th century, it served as the engine of Venetian naval power for over seven centuries—at its peak employing 16,000 workers and capable of producing a fully outfitted warship in a single day.
arsenale.p2: Spanning roughly 45 hectares of covered halls, dry docks, and open yards, the Arsenale is a monumental index of industrial ingenuity. Its massive brick walls, timber-roofed warehouses (tese), and water-accessed basins represent a proto-industrial system that anticipated modern assembly-line production by centuries.
arsenale.p3: Since 1980, the Arsenale has served as a primary exhibition site for the La Biennale di Venezia—its raw, monumental spaces providing a counterpoint to the refined galleries of the Giardini. National pavilions, large-scale installations, and the central International Exhibition share this vast industrial landscape, transforming shipbuilding halls into some of the most powerful exhibition spaces in the world.
arsenale.p4: Tesa 41 sits within this historic matrix—one of the original covered warehouses now given over to artistic production. The Armenian Pavilion's presence continues a tradition of nations working within the Arsenale's industrial grain, not against it.
